title.narrative: RAINWATER HARVESTING AND STORAGE AT HOME

description.narrative: Maji Nyumbani feasibility phaseWhere small, piped schemes exist in rural communities, they are often managed by voluntary “self-help” groups or micro-entrepreneurs who start by coming together to pool their own little cash contributions to start as a social project to address a felt need. And gradually, they struggle to scale operations due to lack of financing opportunities to invest in infrastructure, ending up providing unreliable service. Quite often, intermittent funding from Government and NGOs are the only financing sources for such social enterprises.Savings and Credit Cooperatives (SACCOs) are the most dominant social finance intermediaries in these rural communities – and better placed to provide tailored financing solutions for these underserved households and community-based water enterprises. Their mode of operations “self-help financing” replicates the practice of vast households and self-help groups in rural villages. However, the opportunity for SACCOs to play a financing role for water investment needs in local communities, remains un-explored despite majority of the households and micro enterprises being members/or clients of SACCOs in such rural setting in Kenya.KUSCCO’S _Maji Nyumbani _programme aims to catalyze provision of micro-loans for drinking water and sanitation assets and infrastructure at home through SACCOs in Kenya.In its implementation phase, the program will build capacities of select SACCOs with national reach to provide water/sanitation financing solutions for both households and community-based water enterprises active in their locality. SACCOs will receive technical assistance from the program to develop water loan products that respond to the needs of their members and communities, activate demand through promotions and targeted incentives, and lend with own capital as proof of concept. The project will apply a portion of its resources to incentivize SACCOs to mobilize finance and investment towards WASH products, as a part of our effort to mobilize KES 1.12B in financing over two years (to be verified) from the 10 proposed SACCOs. The incentive will be used for marketing purposes and mobilization of funds to ensure availability of affordable loan terms to SACCO clients.The feasibility study will analyze examples of incentives and market mobilization in the cooperative sector that have been successful and recommend for adoption.

The program will target households and community-based water /sanitation service providers and other micro businesses. Specific needs of each customer segment will be elaborated from the feasibility study and market analysis to be carried out by the program before roll-out. We expect these needs to fall in two categories:++Home Water Investments++: These will include investments in water tanks and water harvesting equipment, home water purifiers, solar powered water booster-pumps, fittings, piped connections, toilets. We expect SACCO members to be the main borrowers, with loan sizes of about KES 20K.++Assets and micro-projects++: Micro enterprises may require short-term working capital to stock water /sanitation related projects of implement micro projects in their communities. Important assets may include water tanks, pipes, meters, gutters, solar panels, pumps, purifiers, chlorines, etc. Micro-projects will mainly revolve around water connections to households.Once there is proof of demand and interest from SACCOs to scale lending, KUSCCO will support with raising required financing through its CCF facility; with an aim to blend SACCO savings and external finance.

title.narrative: 1- Improved access to safe water, sanitation and IWRM services/products
S1- Total number of current unique users served by the initiative with access to improved and safe sanitation products and services

description.narrative: Fill in total number of unique current users for sanitation. Disaggregated per: Male/Female. Type: Domestic users (private and households), school users and for other public users (e.g markets and hospitals, communal users etc) Finally disaggregate users that are provided with a Safely managed / Basic service / Limited service from the initiative. The initiative must tick all criteria to be considered as that service level. 1) Safely managed service: - the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs) - the initiative's sanitation service is not shared with other households - the initiative ensures that human excreta are safely disposed in situ or transported and treated off-site 2) Basic service: - the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs) - the initiative's sanitation facility is not shared with other households - initiative does not ensure that human excreta and urine is safely disposed / transported / treated 3) Limited service: Usually at baseline level, but cannot be included at target level. This includes, open pits, unimproved pit latrines, unlined pits, no slabs, prone to flooding etc \* This is indicative of the reach and scale of the initiative in reaching new users with its products and services in terms of the service level that is being provided (as defined by JMP).

description.narrative: Total nr of beneficiaries disaggregated by Male/Female and Domestic/school/public users Please also check the criteria per service level to see what level best matches your initiative. The initiative must fulfill all criteria to be considered at that service level. 1. Safely managed service: 2. the initiative provides an improved source of water (this includes: piped water, boreholes or tube wells, protected dug wells, protected springs, rainwater, packaged / bottled water, water that is delivered) 3. the initiative is located on the premises of the household or dwelling 4. the initiative provides drinking water whenever it is needed 5. the drinking water provided by the initiative has no presence of E.coli 6. the drinking water provided by the initiative contains no / limited levels of arsenic and fluoride (below WHO standards: < 0.01 mg/L arsenic and < 1.5mg/L fluoride 7. Basic service: 8. the initiative provides an improved source of water (this includes: piped water, boreholes or tube wells, protected dug wells, protected springs, rainwater, packaged / bottled water, water that is delivered) 9. the initiative provides water for users where the collection time is less than 30 minutes for a roundtrip including queuing 0. Limited service: Drinking water from an improved source for which collection time exceeds 30 minutes for a roundtrip including queuing. 1. Unimproved service: Drinking water from an unprotected dug well or unprotected spring \* This is indicative of the reach and scale of the initiative in reaching new users with its products and services in terms of the service level that is being provided (as defined by JMP).
